faq.q: Why does a pendulum stop at the top?
faq.a: At the top all its energy is stored as height and it has no speed left. For a split second it is still, before gravity pulls it back down the other way.
asks: Does a pendulum stop at the end of each swing?

faq.q: Why is a pendulum fastest at the bottom?
faq.a: The bottom is the lowest point, so by then all the height energy has turned into movement energy. That makes it the fastest part of the swing.

faq.q: Why does a pendulum slowly stop?
faq.a: Air resistance and rubbing at the pivot take a little energy every swing, turning it into heat. A pendulum clock keeps going because a spring or falling weight gives it a tiny push each swing.
asks: Why does a swing stop if no one pushes?

faq.q: How do you make a swing go higher?
faq.a: By pushing, or pumping your legs at the right moments, you add energy in time with the swing. Pushes that match its natural rhythm build up big swings, which is called resonance.
asks: Why do you pump your legs on a swing?

faq.q: Does a heavier pendulum swing faster?
faq.a: No. The time for a swing depends on the length of the string, not the weight on the end. A heavy and a light bob on equal strings keep time together.
asks: Does weight change how fast a pendulum swings?

facts: The time a pendulum takes to swing depends on its length, not on the mass of its bob.
Galileo found that, for small swings, each swing of a pendulum takes about the same time whatever its size.

quiz.say: Where in its swing is a pendulum moving fastest?
quiz.why: At the lowest point all the height energy has turned into movement energy, so the speed is greatest.

wrong.0: At the highest point it stops for an instant.
wrong.2: Halfway up, some energy is still stored as height, so it is slower than at the bottom.
